AZULEJO EDITORIAL

Treats the tile as ornament, not wallpaper: deep aubergine masthead, then the azulejo appears only as narrow inlay bands marking each section break. Asymmetric hero with the photo bleeding off the right edge. Squared 2px buttons, hairline-ruled testimonials, full-bleed article split.

Why: most distinctive, and the Portuguese identity is structural rather than decorative.
Tradeoff: the art direction needs discipline to maintain — every new section has to earn its band.

QUIET LUXURY

Cream page, aubergine ink, purple reserved for small accents. Cormorant Garamond display over Raleway small caps. Azulejo stays present but whispered: a framed inlay band under the wordmark, a tile strip running alongside each photo, and a very faint watermark behind the philosophy and CTA panels.

Why: reads most expensive and most grown-up; closest to a boutique print identity.
Tradeoff: the least colourful of the three — loses some of the current warmth and energy.

SOFT BOUTIQUE

The most polished version of what the site already is: soft lavender field, white rounded cards with long soft shadows, floating pill nav, pill CTAs. Azulejo carried as a tinted wash behind the masthead, CTA and footer, plus a tile cap on each testimonial card.

Why: safest to adopt — closest to today's structure, biggest polish gain per unit of change.
Tradeoff: least distinctive; the card-and-shadow language is common on modern service sites.
